Compare peptide-level HDX uptake across three or more protein states

Source: R/compare_states_tp.R
compare_states_tp.Rd

Every other significance function in this package (plot_fissure_vent(), diff_peptides_prep(), robot_indexes()) compares exactly two states at a time. This function does two things for three or more states: (1) an omnibus test per peptide across all requested states (does this peptide differ across any of them at all) - by default a Welch one-way ANOVA (stats::oneway.test(), unequal variances), reported but not used to gate significance (see Details) - and (2) the package's usual Hageman & Weis hybrid test (pooled CI_2pts() + per-pair Welch p-value) for every pair of states (or every reference vs. the rest, if reference is given). A pair is significant when its Welch p-value (raw by default, or adjusted with p_adjust across the peptides of that pair) is below pvalue AND its difference exceeds the pooled CI - the same rule as every other function in the package.

Usage

compare_states_tp(
  filepath,
  times,
  states = NULL,
  by = c("sequence", "position"),
  reference = NULL,
  regions = NULL,
  replicates = NULL,
  alpha = 0.01,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  p_adjust = "none",
  omnibus = c("welch", "kruskal"),
  percent = FALSE,
  p_adjust_method
)

Arguments

filepath

filepath to the input file (same format as output_tp()/nm_states() expect) - this function calls output_tp() internally, once per pair plus once for all states together, rather than taking an already-built wide table, precisely because that wide format has already discarded the availability information available-case matching needs (see Details).

times

a single Deut.Time value to compare at.

states

character vector of three or more states to compare. Default NULL uses every state found in filepath (nm_states()).

by

matching rule for identifying "the same peptide" across states. "sequence" (default) requires identical Sequence, Start, End and Charge in both states (output_tp()'s seq_match = FALSE). "position" matches on Start, End and Charge only, ignoring Sequence (output_tp()'s seq_match = TRUE), so a peptide covering a point mutation is still compared; its Sequence is then reported as the per-state sequences joined by ".". In both modes peptide_id is Start_End_zCharge (plus the sequence in "sequence" mode), so each charge state is its own peptide.

reference

optional state name. If given, only reference vs. each other state is tested (N-1 pairs, Dunnett-style), instead of every pair (N(N-1)/2) - both fewer simultaneous tests and usually the actually-relevant contrast for a wild-type/apo vs. several perturbations design. Default NULL tests every pair.

regions

optional named list of c(start, end) residue ranges (e.g. list(NTR = c(1, 85), ACD = c(86, 165))). When supplied, only peptides fully contained in a region (Start >= start & End <= end) are compared, run separately per region, and the result gets a region column. Default NULL compares every peptide with no filtering (no region column in the output).

replicates

optional maximum number of replicates per state (passed to output_tp()). Default NULL uses every replicate; states may differ.

alpha

alpha for the pooled critical interval (CI_2pts()), applied per pair. Default 0.01.

pvalue

significance cutoff applied to the per-pair p-value (raw, or adjusted with p_adjust). Default 0.01.

p_adjust

multiple-testing correction passed to stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default, raw Welch p-values, as in every other function) or e.g. "BH". Pairwise p-values are adjusted across the peptides of each pair of states (the same family as everywhere in the package); the omnibus p-values are adjusted across peptides.

omnibus

omnibus test across all states per peptide: "welch" (default, Welch one-way ANOVA) or "kruskal" (Kruskal-Wallis).

percent

passed to output_tp() - FALSE (default) compares uptake in Daltons, TRUE percent deuteration, "FD" percent of the fully deuterated control, "per_residue" uptake per exchangeable amide (removes peptide length from the critical-interval condition).

p_adjust_method

deprecated; earlier versions adjusted with p_adjust_method = "BH" by default. Supplying it sets p_adjust, with a warning.

Value

data.frame with one row per peptide-by-state-pair (by region, if regions is supplied): peptide_id, Start, End, Sequence, state1, state2, delta (state2 - state1), p_value (raw per-pair Welch p-value), ci (pooled CI for that pair), p_adj (per-pair p-value after p_adjust; equal to p_value when "none"), p_omnibus/p_omnibus_adj (NA for peptides absent from at least one requested state), and is_sig.

Which replicate SD feeds the pooled CI

Each state's own raw replicate SD, pooled via CI_2pts() - the same threshold as plot_fissure_vent()'s default (sd_source = "raw"), CI_tp(), diff_peptides_prep() and the interactive plots, so ci values here match those functions for the same pair (when those are given a table of the same two states; on a table of 3+ states they pool over the peptides found in every state, so the CI can differ slightly). It treats every state symmetrically and needs no reference state.

Available-case, not complete-case, matching

output_tp()'s wide-format merge is an inner join across every state passed to it - a peptide missing from any one of N states is dropped entirely, so calling output_tp() once with all N states would silently shrink the comparable peptide set combinatorially as N grows (a peptide identified in 90% of runs per state survives in only 0.9^N of cases). This function instead calls output_tp() separately per pair, so a peptide only needs to be present in the two states of that specific pair to be tested there - "available-case" matching. The one place complete-case is unavoidable is the omnibus test itself: it cannot test a peptide against a group it has no data for, so the omnibus p-value is computed from the peptide set present in all requested states (via one additional output_tp() call with every state), and peptides outside that set simply get NA in p_omnibus/p_omnibus_adj.

The omnibus test

The default omnibus test is a Welch one-way ANOVA, which keeps useful power at the small replicate counts typical of HDX (3 per state). The rank-based Kruskal-Wallis test (omnibus = "kruskal") is available but is very coarse at this size: with 3 states of 3 replicates its smallest attainable p-value is about 0.0036. Either way the omnibus p-value is reported for context (p_omnibus, and p_omnibus_adj adjusted across peptides with p_adjust); is_sig depends only on the per-pair rule.

See also

plot_fissure_vent(), diff_peptides_prep(), CI_2pts(), compare_states_unmatched()

Examples

# \donttest{
file_3state <- system.file("extdata", "three_states.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
res <- compare_states_tp(file_3state, times = "1800.00s", reference = "WT_pH7.5")
